narratives.Description: design(agents-md): relocate policy bulk out of the always-on surface into on-demand skills + cross-harness plugins (post-#1882)
narratives.Overview:
## Problem / context

Umbrella #1882 ("AGENTS.md is a map, not a manual") ran the prose-diet play to completion: freeze/ratchet (#645), skill-routing → REFERENCES (#838), rationale-collapse (#2156), platform-conditional lazy-load (#2157), consumer advisory guardrail (#2155), structure guidance (#646/#647). It reduced the maintainer file 569 → ~470 lines and holds the line via `verify:agents-md-budget`.

That work met its goal — and it was not enough. The **consumer-projected managed section is still ~28.5 KB**, and it still reads as "too complex" at the leadership level. The signal from #1882 is structural: incremental trimming *within the always-on-markdown paradigm* has plateaued. Peer agent frameworks bootstrap with a fraction of this footprint (order-of-magnitude smaller always-on surface, bulk loaded on demand; exact numbers to be measured in Child A). The remaining lever is not more trimming — it is **where policy lives**.

## Goal

Move rule *bulk* off the always-on surface into on-demand skills and cross-harness plugins, so the always-on entry becomes a thin map of pointers. #1882 dieted the prose; this epic changes the delivery architecture.

## Non-goals

- Deleting capabilities. Focus ≠ delete — the full catalog stays; it stops loading by default.
- Re-opening or re-litigating #1882's completed line reductions.
- Committing to a single packaging vendor before the spike (Child A) reports.

## Principle for approval (@visionik)

This epic asks @visionik to ratify a **product boundary principle**, independent of the exact mechanics below. **Status: P1–P3 approved by @visionik 2026-07-06.**

- **P1 — Thin always-on / thick on-demand.** The always-on surface is a map of pointers; policy bulk lives in skills/plugins/packs.
- **P2 — Explicit tiering.** Daily core → standard skills → advanced → deferred.
- **P3 — Context budget is a first-class release gate.** (Instrument decided in Child C; see below.)

## Approach

Tier the existing surface, then relocate:

- **Daily core** — thin always-on pointers only (orient / configure / scope / build / review entrypoints).
- **Standard / advanced** — on-demand skills and/or cross-harness plugins.
- **Deferred** — docs-only or paused (starting candidates: the 8 deprecated `deft-*` skill redirect stubs).

Two mechanisms currently *block* this and must change first: the propagation contract that forces full-text rule mirroring into the always-on file (Child B), and the absence of a behavior-regression gate on rule relocation (Child D).

## Design decisions (approved)

These refine *how* P1–P3 are implemented. **Status: DD-1–DD-3 approved by @visionik 2026-07-06** ("DD-1 through DD-3 sound good").

- **DD-1 — Content-type-keyed hybrid, not "everything to skills."** Route relocation by content type, not one mechanism for all: workflow procedures → **skills** (native frontmatter routing + cross-harness distributable); cross-cutting guardrails → **deterministic `task` gates + a terse always-on imperative**; reference/rationale → **lazy doc tree** (main.md/docs/packs), pointer-only. "Everything to skills" is a category error for guardrails, because skill loading is model-discretionary and a guardrail that only fires when the model chooses to load it is a safety regression.
- **DD-2 — Tier the non-skill items by trigger frequency.** *Universal* guardrails (fire every session / every code change — branch policy, implementation-intent, deterministic-questions, session-start ritual) keep a one-line always-on imperative + gate pointer. *Contextual* guardrails (fire only in a specific runtime/task — PowerShell encoding, SCM-boundary, safe-subprocess, cascade automation) move to the lazy doc tree behind a runtime-detect pointer (precedent: #2157 relocated the PowerShell rules exactly this way). *Reference* always lazy. This holds the always-on floor to "N-universal-guardrails × 1 line," not paragraphs — the lazy doc tree absorbs all reference AND all contextual guardrails, but universal guardrails retain a small irreducible always-on floor by design.
- **DD-3 — The budget counts injected skill frontmatter, not just AGENTS.md bytes.** On native-skill harnesses the harness injects every skill's frontmatter description into each session — that is always-on context. "Move to skills" hides bloat rather than removing it unless Child C's budget and Child A's per-harness measurement include injected frontmatter.
- **Q1 (skill references in AGENTS.md):** AGENTS.md should NOT enumerate skills — native frontmatter handles discovery (contingent on Child A for non-native harnesses). AGENTS.md keeps only a one-line "scan skills before improvising" behavioral nudge.

## Children

- **A — #2370** — Packaging spike: cross-harness skill distribution; OpenPackage vs Bridge-native; distribution-layer vs runtime-router; measure per-harness bootstrap cost. Research → recommendation, no code.
- **B — #2371** — Invert the agents-entry propagation contract (#2111) from full-text-mirror to pointer-sufficient. Wave 1 prerequisite for relocation.
- **C — #2372** — Decide the context-budget instrument (relative ratchet #645 vs absolute); recommended potential target ≤8 KB / ~2k tok, left open.
- **D — #2373** — Eval-health regression gate on every rule-relocation PR; the safety net for moving *rules* (not just rationale).
- Relocation execution slices — filed after B (#2371) + C (#2372) land.

## Wave order

- **Wave 1 (unblock):** #2371 (contract inversion); #2372 (budget target decision); delete the deprecated skill stubs.
- **Wave 2 (relocate, each PR gated by #2373):** move rule bulk → skills/packs, leaving thin pointers.
- **Wave 3 (packaging):** act on #2370's recommendation.
- Waves 1–2 are blocked on @visionik approval of P1–P3.

## Definition of done

- Always-on managed section reduced to a thin pointer surface (target per Child C).
- No enforceable rule lost — every relocated rule reachable via skill/pack/gate.
- `eval:health` shows no regression across the relocation (Child D).
- Cross-harness distribution decision recorded (Child A).

## Risks / open questions

- **OQ-1 (Child C):** relative ratchet (#645, current design) vs absolute target. Recommendation: add an absolute north-star (≤8 KB / ~2k tok) *below* the current ratchet; keep the ratchet as the anti-inflation floor. Left open for decision.
- **Behavioral regression:** relocating *rules* (vs #1882's rationale) is a real behavior change; Child D is the safety net.
- **Vendor dependency:** Child A must weigh OpenPackage longevity/lock-in vs a Deft-owned path.

## References

- Predecessor: #1882 (completed AGENTS.md prose-diet; ratchet at managed 205 / unmanaged 266).
- Freeze gate: `verify:agents-md-budget` (#645).
- Propagation contract: `agents_entry_contract.test.ts` (#2111).
- Consumer advisory: `agentsMdAdvisory` (#2155).

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @visionik (2026-07-06T18:59:07Z)

I approve P1-P3.   

I have some lingering questions we should discuss:

1. Does AGENTS.md need references to skills; or should the frontmatter of the skills handle that?

2. What are the pros and cons of a) trying to move everything to skills vs b) continuing to use the lazy-loaded tree of main.md based directive markdown files?



### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-07-06T19:36:05Z)

Thanks @visionik — P1–P3 recorded as approved. Answers to your two questions, and I've recorded a proposed design decision (DD-1–DD-3) in the epic body for your buy-in.

**Q1 — does AGENTS.md need skill references, or does frontmatter handle it?** Mostly frontmatter. On a native-skill harness the frontmatter *is* the routing surface — the harness injects each skill's name/description into every session, so a hand-maintained list in AGENTS.md is redundant and rots (this is what #838 started by moving the routing table to the REFERENCES Skills Index). AGENTS.md should keep only a one-line "scan skills before improvising" behavioral nudge, not an enumeration. Two caveats: (1) that nudge is a behavior no single skill's frontmatter encodes, so it survives; (2) harnesses with no native skill discovery need a fallback pointer — which is exactly what Child A (#2370) resolves. So the answer is contingent on Child A.

**Q2 — everything-to-skills (a) vs lazy main.md tree (b)?** It's a false binary; the right cut is by content type (proposed as DD-1):

| Content type | Home | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow procedures (setup, build, review-cycle, swarm, release, triage) | Skills | Native routing + cross-harness distributable |
| Cross-cutting guardrails (branch, encoding, deterministic-questions, WIP, story-start) | `task` gates + terse always-on imperative | Enforcement can't be discretionary |
| Reference / rationale | Lazy doc tree (b), pointer-only | Not workflow, not guardrail |

"Everything to skills" is a category error for guardrails: skill loading is model-discretionary, and a guardrail that only fires when the model chooses to load it is a safety regression.

**On the tiering follow-up (does the non-skill bulk re-bog AGENTS.md?)** — recorded as DD-2. Reference costs zero always-on (fully lazy). Guardrails have an irreducible always-on floor because their *pre-gate steering* must fire before the gate does — but we hold that floor small by (1) compressing each to one imperative line + gate pointer and (2) tiering guardrails by trigger frequency: universal ones stay always-on as one-liners; contextual ones (PowerShell, SCM-boundary, cascade) move to the lazy doc tree behind a runtime-detect pointer — precedent #2157. So the lazy doc tree gets *stronger* (absorbs all reference + all contextual guardrails); only universal guardrails keep a small always-on floor by design.

**One catch worth your eye (DD-3):** "move to skills" does not shrink the always-on budget if the harness injects all skill frontmatter every session — so the budget gate (Child C) and Child A's measurement must count injected frontmatter, not just AGENTS.md bytes, or we relocate bloat instead of removing it.

Requesting your buy-in on **DD-1 / DD-2 / DD-3** as the implementation shape for P1–P3.


### Comment by @visionik (2026-07-06T20:11:30Z)

DD-1 through DD-3 sound good
